testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What do Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) do?

options.text: They reduce a vehicle's braking power.
They work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
They do not work on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works alongside a vehicle's normal brakes. It does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS only activates when the wheels are about to lock up.

questions.question: What does the air compressor do in a truck with air brakes?

options.text: It pumps air into the storage tanks.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks. The compressor is controlled by the governor.

questions.question: What are alcohol evaporators used for?

options.text: They add alcohol to the brake system to prevent freezing.
They are only allowed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: They add alcohol to the brake system to prevent freezing.
questions.explanation: Alcohol evaporators add alcohol to the air brake system. This prevents ice from forming and damaging the brakes.

questions.question: How long should it take for air pressure to build up in a single air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three minutes
questions.explanation: In a single air brake system, the pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within three minutes after the engine reaches normal speed.

questions.question: What is true about a dual air brake system?

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.
Only the brakes on one side of the vehicle work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: Heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. Each system has its own air tanks. The two systems share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: They allow rain water to enter the tanks.
They remove water and oil from the tanks.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the system. If water and oil build up, they can damage the air brakes.

questions.question: What should you do before inspecting slack adjusters on S-cam brakes?

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes.
Put on gloves and push in the slack adjusters.
Remove the drum and look inside.
Block the wheels and turn off the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block the wheels and turn off the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, block the wheels, and turn off the parking brake. Then pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should not move more than about one inch. If it moves more, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: How often should you check the alcohol evaporator in cold weather?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every day
questions.explanation: In cold weather, check and refill the alcohol evaporator every day. This prevents ice from building up in the air brake system.

questions.question: What should you do if the spring brakes are on?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.
Be careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not apply the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve allows a driver to slowly apply spring brakes. It is controlled by a lever on the dashboard in equipped vehicles.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle, the maximum air leakage during an applied leakage test is ____ in one minute.
questions.correctAnswerText: 6 psi
questions.explanation: You need to know the safe maximum air loss rate for your vehicle type. A triple combination vehicle must not lose more than 6 psi of air pressure in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are used:

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: At each wheel.
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes work at every wheel on the vehicle. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.correctAnswerText: Modulating control valve
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. In vehicles that have this feature, a lever on the dashboard controls it.

questions.question: Brakes that are out of adjustment will:

options.text: Make some brakes work too hard and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make some brakes work too hard and fail.
questions.explanation: Brakes that are out of adjustment will wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check your brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: Every vehicle with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If this signal goes off while driving, stop the vehicle right away and have the system fixed.

questions.question: Front wheel brakes will work:
questions.correctAnswerText: In all conditions.
questions.explanation: Front wheel brakes work well on any road surface. You are unlikely to skid with your front wheels, even on ice.

questions.question: Brake fading happens when:

options.text: Brakes are not used often enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes overheat.
questions.explanation: Using brakes too much causes them to get too hot and become less effective. This is called brake fading.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning signal goes off while driving, you should:

options.text: Leave the road safely as soon as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the road safely as soon as possible
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning goes off while driving, safely exit the road and park as soon as you can. If air pressure gets too low, your brakes will not stop the vehicle safely.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in very wet weather when it is freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly let go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: When using parking brakes in very wet, freezing weather, the moisture can freeze and lock the brakes, making the vehicle unable to move.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to show the system is not working right.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System warning lights are usually yellow. If the ABS stops working, your vehicle will still have normal brakes.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if you push the green lever on the control panel.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a short delay.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with air brakes, it takes about half a second or longer for air to travel through the lines and activate the brakes. This is different from hydraulic brakes in cars and smaller trucks, which work instantly.

questions.question: You need an air brake endorsement to:

options.text: Drive a vehicle with air brakes.
Drive any truck with a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes knowledge test to get a license to operate any vehicle with air brakes. This includes systems that use air over hydraulic brakes.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.correctAnswerText: Inside
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the vehicle's axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are located inside the brake drum.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle, the maximum air leakage during a test is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 6 psi per minute.
questions.explanation: You need to know the maximum safe air loss for your vehicle type. A triple combination vehicle must not lose more than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: Why should you drain the air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because air gets old and needs to be replaced.
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil that build up in the air storage tanks and can damage the brake system. You should drain the tanks to remove these materials. If your tank has a manual drain valve, drain it at the end of each day of driving.
